info.title: dotnet-bld
info.description: Tool to clean build output folders for msbuild, dotnet build

commands.name: build-props
commands.description: Analyze Directory.Build.props files and property provenance across projects. (BETA)

options.name: --markdown
options.description: Emit markdown table output where supported.

options.name: --root
options.description: Root directory, .sln, or project file. Can also be specified as trailing argument.

options.name: --depth
options.description: If root is a directory, recursion depth to search for .sln or project files. [default: 3]

options.name: --list
options.description: Only list imported Directory.Build.props files in a tree structure, without showing property contents.

options.name: --no-overridden
options.description: Hide properties that originate from Directory.Build.props but are overridden later in evaluation.

options.name: --properties
options.description: Comma-separated list of properties to trace (e.g., TargetFramework,Nullable). When specified, only shows these properties.

options.name: --verbosity
options.description: Log verbosity (Debug, Verbose, Info, Warning, Error). [default: Warning]

options.name: --vstoolspath
options.description: Explicit value for VSToolsPath. If not specified, the tool tries to resolve VSToolsPath either from environment variable or via vswhere.exe. VSToolsPath contains additional msbuild target files which may be required for evaluation of project files.

options.name: --novstoolspath
options.description: Do not try to resolve VSToolsPath from ENV or vswhere.exe.

options.name: --concurrency
options.description: Degree of parallelism for project evaluation. Use 1 for sequential processing. [default: 2]

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help and usage information

commands.name: clean
commands.description: Cleans solution / project build output (bin/obj etc.)

options.name: --root
options.description: Root directory, .sln, or project file. Can also be specified as trailing argument.

options.name: --depth
options.description: If root is a directory, recursion depth to search for .sln or project files. [default: 3]

options.name: --noncurrent
options.description: Only clean directories for non-current target frameworks.
Also clean BaseIntermediateOutputPath (obj folder).

options.name: --keep-assets
options.description: When cleaning obj, preserve NuGet restore artifacts (project.assets.json etc.) and only delete build output subdirectories.

options.name: --publish
options.description: Also clean publish output (PublishDir) and pack output (PackageOutputPath), including artifacts/publish and artifacts/package in the artifacts layout.

options.name: --test-results
options.description: Also clean TestResults directories (dotnet test output: .trx, coverage) next to each project and its solution.

options.name: --interactive
options.description: Pick the directories from a list grouped by project: b/o/p/g/t toggle bin, obj, publish, package and test results for every project on the top line or for one project on its line, space toggles a directory, enter confirms. --obj/--publish/--test-results only decide what starts out checked. Deletes what was picked after one confirmation; pass --output-file to write the script instead. On by default unless --delete or --output-file is given; needs an interactive terminal. [default: true]

options.name: --keep-private-packages
options.description: Before cleaning, copy every package restored from a source other than nuget.org from the NuGet packages folder into a folder feed and write nuget.offline.config next to the root, pointing those sources at it. Keeps the repo restorable after the private feed is gone and the caches are cleared. Needs a prior restore. The same step as `nuget keep`.

options.name: --private-packages-dir
options.description: Folder for --keep-private-packages (default: .nuget-private in the root directory).

options.name: --verbosity
options.description: Log verbosity (Debug, Verbose, Info, Warning, Error). [default: Warning]

options.name: --output-file
options.description: Write a deletion script instead of deleting (clean.cmd or clean.sh when no path is given). [default: clean.sh]

options.name: --yes
options.description: Do not ask for confirmation (requires explicit root). --yes/-y is the same switch, as in `outdated undo`.

options.name: --vstoolspath
options.description: Explicit value for VSToolsPath. If not specified, the tool tries to resolve VSToolsPath either from environment variable or via vswhere.exe. VSToolsPath contains additional msbuild target files which may be required for evaluation of project files.

options.name: --novstoolspath
options.description: Do not try to resolve VSToolsPath from ENV or vswhere.exe.

options.name: --concurrency
options.description: Degree of parallelism for project evaluation. Use 1 for sequential processing. [default: 2]

options.name: --delete
options.description: Delete without the picker, asking per directory unless --force is given.

options.name: --confirm
options.description: Confirmation Level for deletion. [default: Directory]

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help and usage information

commands.name: containerize
commands.description: Analyze Dockerfiles and .NET projects with SDK container build properties (PublishProfile=DefaultContainer, ContainerBaseImage, ContainerFamily, ContainerRepository, ...), or migrate Dockerfiles to those properties.

options.name: --markdown
options.description: Emit markdown table output where supported.

options.name: --root
options.description: Root directory, .sln, or project file. Can also be specified as trailing argument.

options.name: --depth
options.description: If root is a directory, recursion depth to search for .sln or project files. [default: 3]

options.name: --verbosity
options.description: Log verbosity (Debug, Verbose, Info, Warning, Error). [default: Warning]

options.name: --list
options.description: Only list Dockerfiles without parsing details.

options.name: --projects
options.description: Scan for .NET projects with container build properties.

options.name: --all
options.description: Scan for both Dockerfiles and .NET container projects.

options.name: --migrate
options.description: Migrate each Dockerfile to SDK container properties (ContainerBaseImage, ContainerPort, ContainerEnvironmentVariable, ...) on the project it builds. Dry run unless --apply is given.

options.name: --apply
options.description: With --migrate, write the properties into the project files (default is dry-run).

options.name: --delete-dockerfile
options.description: With --migrate --apply, delete the migrated Dockerfile and remove the Visual Studio container-tools settings (Docker* properties, Microsoft.VisualStudio.Azure.Containers.Tools.Targets) from the project.

options.name: --force
options.description: With --migrate, migrate a Dockerfile even when its runtime stage has instructions the SDK cannot express (RUN, VOLUME, HEALTHCHECK, files copied from the build context). They are listed and dropped. --force is the old name for this option.

options.name: --run-as-root
options.description: With --migrate, write ContainerUser=root for a Dockerfile without USER instead of asking. Without it the question is asked per Dockerfile; when it cannot be asked the SDK's default user (non-root app on .NET 8+ images) is kept.

options.name: --validate
options.description: Check the SDK container settings of each project: names the SDK does not read, the obsolete ContainerImageName, deprecated ContainerEntrypoint items, invalid values, a ContainerBaseImage the SDK computes anyway or a family variant of it (ContainerFamily). With --apply, rewrite the findings that have an exact equivalent.

options.name: --enable
options.description: Enable SDK container publishing for the apps under the root that have no container settings yet, so `dotnet publish /t:PublishContainer` builds their image: EnableSdkContainerSupport in each project, and the settings all of them share (ContainerFamily, the runtime identifier(s), ContainerRegistry, ContainerImageTags) in Directory.Build.props or the projects. Their defaults are your last interactive answers (container.json under BLD_HOME), then what Directory.Build.props already sets, then --family/--rid/--registry/--image-tags. Libraries, test projects, projects with container settings and .NET Framework targets are listed with the reason they are skipped. Dry run unless --apply is given; -i asks the shared settings once, with the defaults preselected, then per app.

options.name: --family
options.description: With --enable, the ContainerFamily: the variant of the image the SDK picks (alpine, noble, noble-chiseled, noble-chiseled-extra, azurelinux3.0, azurelinux3.0-distroless, azurelinux3.0-distroless-extra; any other tag suffix is written as given), or 'default' for the SDK's Debian image. With -i, skips that question.

options.name: --rid
options.description: With --enable, the runtime identifier of the image (ContainerRuntimeIdentifier, e.g. linux-arm64, linux-musl-x64 for alpine). Several, repeated or ';'-separated, make one multi-platform image (ContainerRuntimeIdentifiers, with RuntimeIdentifiers covering them). With -i, skips that question.

options.name: --registry
options.description: With --enable, the ContainerRegistry to push to (host, with port if any); an empty value means none, the image goes to the local daemon. With -i, skips that question.

options.name: --image-tags
options.description: With --enable, the ContainerImageTags (';'-separated, $(Version) allowed); an empty value means the SDK's 'latest'. With -i, skips that question.

options.name: --build-props
options.description: With --enable, write the shared settings into Directory.Build.props (the one the projects import, or a new one in the root), where every project below gets them, and only EnableSdkContainerSupport into each app. Without -i the settings go into each app; with -i this is asked, defaulting to yes for more than one app or an existing Directory.Build.props.

options.name: --interactive
options.description: With --migrate or --validate, ask per Dockerfile or finding and write the answers: whether to migrate a Dockerfile (and drop what the SDK cannot express, and delete it afterwards), which findings to fix. Writes without --apply.

commands.name: keep
commands.description: Keep the packages the projects restored from a source other than nuget.org in a folder feed inside the repo and write nuget.offline.config next to it, so they still restore after the private feed is gone and the NuGet caches are cleared: dotnet restore --configfile nuget.offline.config. Which source a package came from is what restore recorded in its .nupkg.metadata; a file nuget.org signed is not kept even when a mirror served it. Needs a prior restore. The same step as clean --keep-private-packages, without the cleaning.

options.name: --dir
options.description: Folder feed to copy the packages into (default: .nuget-private in the root directory). nuget.offline.config is always written in the root directory.

commands.name: outdated
commands.description: Check for outdated NuGet packages and optionally update them to latest versions.

options.name: --markdown
options.description: Emit markdown table output where supported.

options.name: --root
options.description: Root directory, .sln, or project file. Can also be specified as trailing argument.

options.name: --depth
options.description: If root is a directory, recursion depth to search for .sln or project files. [default: 3]

options.name: --apply
options.description: Apply package updates instead of just checking.

options.name: --skip-tfm-check
options.description: Skip target framework compatibility checking when suggesting package updates.

options.name: --prerelease
options.description: Include prerelease versions of NuGet packages.

options.name: --orphaned
options.description: List PackageVersion entries in Directory.Packages.props with no matching PackageReference and a newer version on NuGet. Works for both project and solution input. Report-only.

options.name: --comment-orphans
options.description: On --apply, comment out outdated orphan PackageVersion entries in Directory.Packages.props. Only honored when the input is a solution (.sln / .slnx / .slnf), since a single project cannot see all consumers of the CPM file. Implies --orphaned for reporting.

options.name: --interactive
options.description: Pick the packages to update from a grouped list before applying, and the target version per package (space toggles, left/right change the target, enter confirms, esc cancels). Dependency conflicts between what you picked and what stays are surfaced so you can include the other package, skip the picked one, or accept the risk. Implies --apply. On by default in an interactive terminal unless --apply or --markdown is given; without a terminal the report is printed instead, and an explicit -i fails. [default: true]

options.name: --max-bump
options.description: Largest version step to propose, relative to the version a package is pinned at now: 'major' (no cap), 'minor' (same major, no breaking change per SemVer) or 'patch' (same major and minor). Versions above the cap are reported in the 'held' column instead of being applied. [default: Major]

options.name: --max-bump-for
options.description: Override --max-bump for the packages matching a pattern: "<pattern>=<major|minor|patch>". Same wildcard syntax as --package, may be repeated, accepts ';'-separated lists. The most specific matching pattern wins.

options.name: --group-by
options.description: How --interactive groups the packages it offers: 'prefix' (common package id prefix, the default), 'bump' (patch/minor/major) or 'none' (one flat list). When given explicitly, the report table is grouped the same way. [default: Prefix]

options.name: --group-depth
options.description: Maximum prefix length in dot-separated segments for --group-by prefix. [default: 2]

options.name: --group-min
options.description: Smallest number of packages a --group-by prefix group must have; smaller ones are dissolved into '(other)'. [default: 2]

options.name: --preselect
options.description: Which packages --interactive starts out with a check mark on: 'all' (the default), 'no-major', 'patch' or 'none'. [default: All]

options.name: --package
options.description: Only consider packages whose id matches one of these patterns. Supports '*' wildcards, is case-insensitive, may be repeated, and accepts ';'-separated lists. Default: all packages.

options.name: --exclude
options.description: Skip packages whose id matches one of these patterns. Same syntax as --package and applied after it.

options.name: --allow-conflicts
options.description: Update packages even when a dependency they require stays at a version that does not satisfy their declared range. Without this, such packages are held back.

options.name: --verify-restore
options.description: After --apply, run 'dotnet restore' on the input and fail the command if NuGet reports errors. The only check that sees what NuGet actually resolves.

options.name: --source
options.description: Package source(s) to query: the name of a source in nuget.config or a v3 feed URL. May be repeated. Overrides nuget.config, including package source mapping. Default: the enabled sources from the nuget.config hierarchy, or nuget.org if there is none.

options.name: --ignore-source-mapping
options.description: Query every enabled source for every package instead of honoring the packageSourceMapping section of nuget.config.

options.name: --ignore-policy
options.description: Do not apply the package policy rules saved under BLD_HOME (policy.json) for this run. --max-bump-for still applies.

options.name: --eval-cache
options.description: Skip the MSBuild evaluation of a project configuration when every file that fed its last evaluation is unchanged (kept under BLD_HOME or the local application data folder). Opt-in: MSBuild properties set through environment variables are not detected.

options.name: --verbosity
options.description: Log verbosity (Debug, Verbose, Info, Warning, Error). [default: Warning]

options.name: --vstoolspath
options.description: Explicit value for VSToolsPath. If not specified, the tool tries to resolve VSToolsPath either from environment variable or via vswhere.exe. VSToolsPath contains additional msbuild target files which may be required for evaluation of project files.

options.name: --novstoolspath
options.description: Do not try to resolve VSToolsPath from ENV or vswhere.exe.

options.name: --concurrency
options.description: Degree of parallelism for project evaluation. Use 1 for sequential processing. [default: 2]

commands.name: undo
commands.description: Revert the package updates a previous 'outdated --apply' run wrote to this input. Only values that still read as that run left them are touched; the rest is reported and left alone.

options.name: --root
options.description: Root directory, .sln, or project file. Can also be specified as trailing argument.

options.name: --list
options.description: List the recorded runs for this input, newest first, and exit.

options.name: --run
options.description: Which recorded run to revert: 1 is the newest (the default), 2 the one before, as numbered by --list. [default: 1]

options.name: --package
options.description: Only revert packages whose id matches one of these patterns. Same syntax as outdated --package.

options.name: --exclude
options.description: Leave packages whose id matches one of these patterns as they are. Applied after --package.

options.name: --interactive
options.description: Pick the packages to revert from a grouped list (space toggles, a/n all or none, enter reverts, esc cancels). Needs an interactive terminal.

options.name: --yes
options.description: Revert without asking. Required when there is no interactive terminal.

options.name: --verify-restore
options.description: After reverting, run 'dotnet restore' on the input and fail the command if NuGet reports errors.

options.name: --verbosity
options.description: Log verbosity (Debug, Verbose, Info, Warning, Error). [default: Warning]
